title: Numbers in Chinese Poetry from the Tang Dynasty Onward
description:
A corpus scan of 175,355 classical Chinese poems from the Tang dynasty through the Qing, measuring how often numeral characters appear in shi, ci and qu. 59.24% of poems contain at least one numeral character, and numerals account for 2.15% of all 11,571,489 characters in the corpus. The ci collections sit at the top of the range (71.4% and 71.7%) while shi sits lower (54.8% and 59.0%), and the character 一 is the most frequent numeral in every collection by a wide margin.

The repository releases the counting code, per-poem and per-collection derived datasets, figures, documentation, and the presentation the study originates from. The source corpus is drawn from the open-source chinese-poetry database (MIT License) and is not redistributed; a SHA-256 manifest of every file scanned is included so that any copy can be verified against the one used.

The analysis originates in a digital humanities research presentation given during an exchange program at Peking University in July 2026.
